newsitem.title: USA: Overseas to merge venture with Royal Cruises.
newsitem.headline: Overseas to merge venture with Royal Cruises.

text.p: Overseas Shipholding Group Inc said on Wednesday that Royal Caribbean International increased its offer to acquire Celebrity Cruise Lines to $515 million from $500 million.

The cash portion of the deal was increased to $245 million from $230 million, while the remainder is payable in Royal Caribbean stock, Overseas Shipholding said in a statement about the definitive agreement.
Carnival Corp, which could not be reached for comment, said it had privately offered to buy Celebrity for $510 million in cash earlier in June.
Also, Overseas Shipholding, which owns Celebrity with Chandris Group in a 50-50 joint venture, said Royal Carribean will assume $800 million of Celebrity's debt.
Royal Caribbean said in its original statement on June 17 that the merger would create a fleet of 20 ships, totaling 38,000 berts by the year 2000, including the five vessels currently on order.
Royal Caribbean operates 11 ships and has four ships on order.
